title: kit.upload-record.v1
description: The Evidence record of one upload (@saasreport/uploads): its sha256, what it claimed and what its bytes are, the triage markers, the scanner that ran (name and version; "none" when no scanner is configured), the explicit verdict, the policy that decided and where the object is. There is deliberately no "safe" or "clean" value anywhere: a verdict says what the pipeline did with the file, never that the file is harmless.

version.description: The record's version, assigned by the records sink. Every write is a compare-and-set on it, and a deleted tombstone is final.

last_ref_seq.description: The cursor of person decisions: the highest ledger seq this record has used. A decision is accepted only above it (a replay is never a lower or equal seq), so the record needs no list of every seq ever used.

project.description: A key of the project registry.

form.description: The key of the form in uploads.config.json.

subject_ref.description: The tenant, lead or reference the upload belongs to.

sha256.description: Of the stored bytes (for a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, the bytes up to the container's own end: see trailing_stripped).

trailing_stripped.description: Present when bytes followed the end of a PNG (IEND), JPEG (EOI), GIF (trailer) or WebP (RIFF size). They were cut off before anything was stored or released and are not kept: only their length and the hash of the file as received are.

original_sha256.description: The sha256 of the file as it was received.

filename_full.description: The whole normalised filename (NFKC, no bidi or zero-width characters, no path, no stream suffix): what every rule reads and what a rescan re-evaluates. The display name is filename_normalised.

type.description: From the file's own bytes; application/octet-stream when no signature matched.

matches_declared.description: False when the declared content type or the filename extension names another type than the bytes.

stage.description: The lifecycle state (packages/uploads/lifecycle.json, kit.upload-lifecycle.v1). pending: intake in flight; quarantined: stored, the scan could not be completed; held: waiting for a person; released: copied to the released bucket; blocked: a block verdict; rejected: refused at the edge (nothing stored); deleted: removed, tombstone kept.

op.description: An operation in flight: the intent written BEFORE any object changes and cleared by the commit. A record with an op is never served; the reconciler rolls an interrupted one back or forward.

actor.description: Who caused the transition (the table says which actors may).

fence.description: A fencing token: written into the metadata of every object this operation writes, so a stale settle or a late effect only ever touches objects of its own operation.

verdict.description: allow: nothing found and the scanner said allow. allow_with_limits: released with the serving limits listed. needs_sandbox: cannot be cleared here; opening it needs a sandbox. block. scan_failed: the scan could not be completed (a block, never a pass).

limits.description: The serving limits that come with allow_with_limits (and are kept on needs_sandbox when a form releases it for download).

complete.description: False when a limit or a parse error stopped the analysis: the verdict is then at best needs_sandbox.

statement.description: Fixed text: 'markers found' or 'no known active-content markers found; opening still needs a sandbox'.

incomplete_because.description: Why the analysis is incomplete (a limit, a parse failure).

scanner.description: none when no scanner is configured.

third_party_consent_ref.description: Required when the scanner sends the file to a third party.

key.description: Derived from the record: q/<form>/<sha256>/<upload id>. The original filename is metadata only, never part of a key.

stored.description: False for a file refused at the edge: nothing was written.

decisions.description: A person's decisions on this upload (references to ledger entries), newest last, at most the newest 20: the ledger is the full history, and system bookkeeping lives in the evidence log (kit.upload-evidence.v1), never here.

ref.description: A person's decision is a REFERENCE to the entry of the approval ledger (kit.approval-ledger.v1, <project>:uploads) that holds the signature, the member and the note: nothing signed or free-text is copied into the record, so a tombstone carries no note. One ledger entry is used once.

evidence_ref.description: Pointer into the project's evidence chain.

then.description: With no scanner configured no file is ever allow or allow_with_limits.
